Songwriting & production

  • jump to Songwriting
  • jump to Production
  • jump to Latest releases

I love to make music. I grew up on a diet of Queen, The Rolling Stones, heavy metal, Tchaikovsky and Beethoven. My tastes are a little more varied these days. I'm all about the drama and theatricality to whisk a listener out of their daily lives...

Songwriting

I'm not what you might call a 'normal' songwriter. I like playing different characters, on occasion I even play myself. I'm not interested in being 'cool' - good job, really seeing how I'm just not, never was & never will be.

Here's a load of songs of wildly varying sonic quality. Let me take you on a journey through space and time...

...to a song about that turncoat shit J.D. f-ing Vance, some dance-infused political rock:

And the other of the albums has this gothic house track on it!

In summary

If you've got this far, bloody well done! I just want to create music that is varied and interesting, without worrying about genre or current tastes. If you might want to collaborate then talk to me.

Production

I approach production work with an open mind. Usually with my own material a song will immediately suggest to me what it needs. Sometimes though, you have to be prepared to play to get it to feel right.

Guise

This is a long distance collaboration with an old mate (Jim from uni).

For this one I had the descending bass riff & some idea of the vocal. The drums are painstaking cut up loops. I kept the arrangement sparse to highlight the how the melody, bass and Jim's piano accompaniment worked together.

For this one I wanted acoustic guitars to accompany the voice & a heavy electro-type beat with a big bass for the chorus:

Holy Fools

This was for a now defunct band I was in where we had a load of unused tracking. I wanted to see what I could do with a couple of the recordings, for posterity more than anything. Here's our jazz metal one:

Out of the Rubble

This is my current project where I've done the most production work.

Aliens Stole our Women was a conceptual, collaborative E.P. involving a cast of thousands (well, ten players including me).

This song was quite the production to put together: soooo many parts recorded at different times & in different spaces. It almost works, I properly bit off more than I could chew at the time:

This one's simpler (and arguably more successful):

For this dark, surreal, sometimes mournful, tale from my solo Early Mornings E.P., I wanted the vibe of a film where you're never quite sure what's going on - cue a mash-up of crunchy drums, big synth bass, acoustic and electric guitars:

For the last song on my latest E.P. Channel Surfing, I set myself a challenge of using all 'found' loops, samples and parts. To give it structure I wrote some initial piano chords to hang everything off:

And to end our journey, here's those electro beats again and pile of synths which seemed to suit the rather daft subject matter, from the same E.P.:

Latest releases

I have two new albums coming out in the New Year...

Working title: Odd Pop

A journey through my 30s & a bit of a departure for me - blindingly honest 'pop' about how I felt at the time. It's soul-bearing stuff that I'm nervous to put out.

Working title: Maximum Drama

Ridiculous big stuff drama up to the max. With fat dance breaks & bass. Some choice highlights are:

  • an apocalyptic love affair at the end of the world
  • surviving inside an Assad-like regime in some despotic country
  • embracing your inner chaos

You can't say I didn't warn you! x
